title: Discussion Standard
summary: Professional discussions should create clarity, understanding, solutions, and teamwork — not arguments, gossip, or unnecessary tension.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: Discussions at Zura Spa refer to conversations between therapists, leaders, and other team members concerning work, clients, procedures, challenges, feedback, ideas, and general workplace matters. Professional discussions should create clarity, understanding, solutions, and teamwork—not arguments, gossip, or unnecessary tension.

sections.title: 1. Therapists' Mindset During Discussions
paragraphs: Every therapist should approach a discussion with the mindset: "I am here to understand, contribute, and find a solution—not to win an argument."
Therapists should remember that a discussion is an opportunity to listen, learn, express themselves respectfully, and improve the way the team works.

sections.title: Be Open
paragraphs: Be willing to hear another perspective.

sections.title: Be Calm
paragraphs: Do not allow frustration to control your response.

sections.title: Be Respectful
paragraphs: Disagreement does not justify disrespect.

sections.title: Be Solution-Focused
paragraphs: Focus on what can be done rather than only what went wrong.

sections.title: Be Accountable
paragraphs: Be willing to acknowledge your part when necessary.

sections.title: Be Teachable
paragraphs: Correction is an opportunity to improve, not necessarily a personal attack.

sections.title: Be Professional
paragraphs: Keep personal emotions separate from workplace responsibilities.

sections.title: 2. What Therapists Should Do
paragraphs: During discussions, therapists should:
list: Listen carefully before responding.
Allow others to finish speaking.
Speak clearly and respectfully.
Share relevant facts and information.
Ask questions when something is unclear.
Express concerns through the appropriate channel.
Contribute ideas and possible solutions.
Accept constructive criticism professionally.
Admit mistakes when they occur.
Keep discussions focused on the matter being addressed.
Respect different opinions.
Maintain confidentiality where necessary.
Escalate serious or unresolved matters appropriately.
Leave the discussion with a clear understanding of what is expected next.
sections.closing: A useful approach: LISTEN → UNDERSTAND → RESPOND → SOLVE → ACT.

sections.title: 3. What Therapists Should Not Do
list: Shout, insult, or speak aggressively.
Interrupt repeatedly.
Turn a professional discussion into a personal argument.
Become defensive before understanding the issue.
Attack someone's character instead of addressing the matter.
Use sarcasm, mockery, or humiliation.
Bring unrelated personal issues into the discussion.
Gossip about the discussion afterwards.
Twist information or deliberately misrepresent what was said.
Create sides or encourage other staff to take part in unnecessary conflicts.
Discuss confidential matters with people who do not need to know.
Walk away from an important discussion simply because they disagree.
Refuse to accept reasonable correction.
Agree during the discussion and deliberately ignore the agreed action afterwards.
Use a client's presence as an opportunity to discuss staff or management issues.

sections.title: 4. When Emotions Are High
paragraphs: If a discussion becomes emotionally charged, the therapist should pause rather than react.
Instead of "You always blame me!" say: "I understand the concern. Can we clarify exactly what happened so I can understand what I need to improve?"
Instead of "That's not my problem." say: "Please clarify what you would like me to take responsibility for."
Instead of arguing: "Let's focus on the solution and what should happen going forward."
If the matter cannot be resolved appropriately between the individuals involved, it should be escalated through the proper leadership channel.

sections.title: 5. The Zura Discussion Standard
paragraphs: A successful discussion should end with better understanding, clear expectations, and an appropriate next step.
LISTEN → RESPECT → CLARIFY → CONTRIBUTE → SOLVE → FOLLOW THROUGH

At Zura Spa, therapists are encouraged to speak up, but speak respectfully; disagree, but disagree professionally; receive correction, but don't take it personally; and identify problems, but come with a solution-based mindset.
We don't discuss to prove who is right. We discuss to understand, improve, and move forward.

remember: Discuss to understand, improve, and move forward — not to win an argument.
